findings.claim: The exif.py change alters the behaviour of scanner.py call sites and of the note-image import path that calls register_single_file, without editing them, and test_exif.py does not exercise any of them.
findings.impact: The first scan after deployment writes new file_exif rows, including GPS, for existing HEIC photos and for TIFF, GIF, BMP or other images whose plugin had no _getexif. If this backfill breaks, a library's existing HEIC photos silently stay without Photo Info and no test in test_exif.py fails. It is the only route to EXIF for photos already in a library, because the new upload and copy code only handles new arrivals.
findings.evidence: backend/app/services/scanner.py:387 (register_single_file), :549-552 (backfill for existing rows) and :754 (pass 2 new rows) all call extract_exif. backend/app/services/markdown_image_import.py:416 calls register_single_file. backend/tests/test_exif.py has no test that runs a scan: TestExtractExif and test_exif_is_read_from_every_container call extract_exif directly, and TestEveryWayIn uses upload and copy. A grep for FileExif and extract_exif under backend/tests finds only test_exif.py and the migration tests. docs/process/reviews/fix-heic-exif/decisions.md item (8) records a rescan whose file_exif was identical before and after, so it does not record a backfill of a pre-fix HEIC.
findings.repro: not_reproduced. Mutation by reading only: delete scanner.py:549-552 and no test in test_exif.py reaches that code, so none of them would fail. The full suite was not run.

bucket_proposal.reason: No invariants are declared, so no touch-point list covers these places. The behaviour change looks intended, but the path it depends on has no test in this change.

findings.proposed_fix: Add a test that creates a File row with no FileExif row over a HEIC on disk, runs a scan and asserts the /exif response.

findings.claim: complete_upload calls extract_exif after db.flush(), so reading EXIF happens while the transaction holds the SQLite write lock, and for a PNG with no EXIF before its image data that read decodes the whole image.
findings.impact: While a large PNG is decoded after upload, every other writer waits: other uploads in a batch, comments, progress saves and scans. SQLite's busy wait here is the driver default of 5 seconds, so a very large PNG on slow storage could make a concurrent write fail with 'database is locked'. JPEG and HEIC are not affected, because getexif does not decode their pixels.
findings.evidence: backend/app/services/upload.py:351 flushes and :358 calls extract_exif, with the commit at :371. read_image_dimensions is deliberately called before the flush at :305-307, and the comment at :290-292 keeps the thumbnail generator outside the write lock. backend/app/services/exif.py:70 calls img.getexif(). PngImageFile.getexif calls self.load() when 'exif' is not in info (PIL/PngImagePlugin.py:1097-1101, read in another project's virtualenv, not the pinned Pillow 11.2.1). backend/app/database.py:17 sets only check_same_thread, leaving the driver's default timeout. decisions.md item (6) timed JPEG and HEIC uploads only, not PNG.
findings.repro: not_reproduced. Suggested check: upload a PNG of about 100 MP with no EXIF while another request writes, and time the POST to /complete and the concurrent write, against a build with the extract_exif call moved above the first flush.

bucket_proposal.reason: No invariant is declared. This breaks the local practice of keeping slow file work outside the write lock, and it degrades only under a large PNG with a concurrent writer.

findings.proposed_fix: Call extract_exif next to read_image_dimensions at upload.py:305-307, before any flush on the normal path, and only write the row after the flush.

findings.claim: The diff reaches complete_upload in backend/app/services/upload.py as a new writer and deleter of file_exif rows, and no declared touch-point list names it.
findings.impact: Every image upload now writes file_exif in the upload transaction, and an upload over a reused row deletes that row's old EXIF. The tests and code read correct: the row is replaced in the same transaction and rolls back with it.
findings.evidence: backend/app/services/upload.py:354-360. The reused-row branch keeps the id at :274 and :310-333; a trashed ghost gets a new id at :288-297, and its old row goes through the ON DELETE CASCADE with PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON at backend/app/database.py:35. backend/tests/test_exif.py:206-228 covers replacement and removal on a reused row.
findings.repro: not_reproduced. Reported because no touch-point list exists, not because of a defect.

bucket_proposal.reason: This is an answer to the touch-point question. No invariants file exists, so the place is undeclared.

findings.claim: The diff reaches copy_file in backend/app/services/fileops.py and through it both the single-copy endpoint and batch_copy, as a new writer of file_exif rows, and no declared touch-point list names it.
findings.impact: Each copy, including a copy to another drive, now gets a row copied from the source row rather than read from the copied file. If the source row is stale because the photo was replaced on disk outside the app, the copy inherits the stale values, and the scanner backfill will not correct them because the copy now has a row.
findings.evidence: backend/app/services/fileops.py:298-313, called from backend/app/routers/files.py:505 (batch_copy) and copy_file_endpoint at :1403. Backfill runs only when no row exists: backend/app/services/scanner.py:549. The session has autoflush=False (backend/app/database.py:38), and I found no ordering problem between the File and FileExif inserts by reading. backend/tests/test_exif.py:230-247 tests only a copy in the same folder on the same drive.
findings.repro: not_reproduced. By reading: overwrite a photo on disk outside the app, copy it through the API, then rescan. The copy would show the old photo's EXIF. Before this change it had no row, so a scan would read the bytes actually on disk.

bucket_proposal.reason: This answers the touch-point question. The stale source row itself is a pre-existing limit, and this change only spreads it to copies.

specification_compliance: No invariants file exists for this change, so there is no touch-point list to compare against. Taken literally, every place the diff reaches is outside a list: backend/app/services/exif.py, backend/app/services/upload.py, backend/app/services/fileops.py and backend/tests/test_exif.py, plus the unedited callers in DEEP-1.
docs/specs/INDEX.md has no entry matching exif or heic, and no docs/specs file has either word in its name. No spec was available to judge the change against, so the code was judged on its own.
docs/process/reviews/fix-heic-exif/r1/classification.json lists the same four code paths the diff shows, with risk CRITICAL.

No submodule pointer changes in the diff. A grep under addons/ for file_exif, FileExif, get_ifd, getexif and /exif matched only addons/intelligence/tests/test_vision_worker.py, which builds EXIF bytes for its own fixture.
potential_unspecified_behavior: Upload now extracts EXIF at once and replaces any earlier row for a reused file id; the tests mark this UNSPEC and no spec covers it.
Copy now duplicates the source's file_exif row, including GPS, and sets a new extracted_at on the copy.
Formats whose plugin had no _getexif, such as TIFF, now go through extract_exif successfully and can gain rows. Only JPEG, HEIF and WebP are tested with EXIF.
A photo with no EXIF that replaces one with EXIF on a reused row now loses the old row, so Photo Info disappears.
regression_risks: Scanner race on a reused row: the scanner holds a pending db.merge(FileExif) until its commit at scanner.py:852 or a flush at :744. If complete_upload commits a row for the same id in that window, the scanner's flush could hit a primary-key conflict and fail the scan. This needs an upload over a row with no EXIF that lands during a scan, so it is rare; it is new because upload did not write file_exif before. Not reproduced.

A phone or camera photo whose ISOSpeedRatings holds several values makes int(iso_raw) at exif.py:107 raise, and the outer except drops all EXIF for that photo. This is pre-existing, but this change sends more photos through that line. Not reproduced, and no real phone HEIC was available to the author either (decisions.md, pending).
Copies inherit stale source rows, as described in DEEP-4.
test_coverage: test_exif_is_read_from_every_container covers extract_exif for JPEG, HEIF and WebP, including values in the root, Exif and GPS IFDs. Removing the Exif or GPS IFD read in exif.py would fail it.

TestEveryWayIn covers first upload for JPEG and HEIF, reuse of a row with new EXIF, reuse of a row with no EXIF, and a same-folder copy with and without EXIF. Removing the db.delete at upload.py:356 should fail the re-upload tests through a primary-key conflict.
Not covered: scanner backfill and registration (DEEP-1), a copy to another folder or drive, batch_copy, a row with missing_since set, a trashed ghost, a PNG with an eXIf chunk, and TIFF.
The file_type == 'image' guard at upload.py:358 has no test that would detect its removal. By reading, extract_exif would return None for most non-images anyway.
not_verified: No test, mutation or command was run; this reviewer has read-only tools, so every repro is by reading.
The Pillow behaviour in DEEP-2 was read from a virtualenv of another project on this machine, not the pinned Pillow 11.2.1, and pillow-heif 0.22.0 source was not read.
Actual decode time and lock wait for a large PNG were not measured.
Whether tests outside test_exif.py reach scanner EXIF through the /exif URL was not searched; only FileExif and extract_exif references were.
The commit's contents were not checked with git; the review used the supplied diff and the working tree.
addons/knowledge showed no files in the listing, so it was not checked for EXIF use.
How .avif files open under the pinned libraries, and real phone HEIC files, were not checked.

perspectives.name: scope
perspectives.notes: No touch-point list exists. The second commit widens a HEIC read fix to upload and copy persistence, and the unedited scanner and note-image import paths change behaviour through extract_exif.

perspectives.name: submodules
perspectives.notes: No gitlink change in the diff. No addon reads file_exif or the /exif endpoint, by grep over the populated addons.

perspectives.name: persistence
perspectives.notes: Delete and insert in upload share a transaction, copy inserts share one with the File row, ON DELETE CASCADE is on, and no schema change is made. The one persistence risk is a copy inheriting a stale row.

perspectives.name: concurrency
perspectives.notes: extract_exif runs under the write lock after flush (DEEP-2). A scanner merge can race the new upload insert, recorded as a regression risk.
